sentences.text: Based on the model Stenonychosaurus, this animal measured approximately 2 meters in length, 1 meter in height, and weighed between 27 and 45 kilograms.
It possessed a long neck and long narrow jaws equipped with small sharp teeth.
The creature had long upper limbs that it folded against the chest wall like a bird.
It possessed large sickle-shaped retractable claws on the second toe of each foot, which were raised off the ground when running.
Based on Stenonychosaurus, Troodon is considered one of the most intelligent non-avian dinosaurs.
Researchers suggest that Troodon practiced communal nesting, where multiple females laid eggs together at a single site to form large clutches due to limited individual egg production.
Troodon eggs were characterized by a steep inclination, a trait distinct from both birds and crocodilians.
A parietal bone cataloged as TMP 79.8.1 attributed to Troodon formosus shows a pathological opening that was interpreted as a possible bite wound.
The type species Troodon formosus was discovered in October 1855 and was initially mistaken for a lizard until 1877.
The genus Troodon was named by Leidy in 1856.
Troodon formosus was discovered in 1855 and is one of the first dinosaurs found in North America and Asia.
The name Troodon means wounding tooth in Ancient Greek, referring to the unique serrations on its teeth.
Troodon teeth have prominent ridges oriented apically, a feature distinct from other theropods.
Troodon teeth had large striations with holes at the intersections of denticles, and the denticle points pointed toward the tip of each tooth.
Troodon teeth show wear facets on their sides.
It was proposed that wear patterns on all Troodon teeth suggest a diet based on soft foods, ruling out the consumption of bones, invertebrate exoskeletons, or hard plant matter.
Research hypothesizes that the primary diet of Troodon consisted of meat.
Troodon is believed to have been a predator, supported by its sickle-shaped toe claw and good binocular vision.
It was likely an agile hunter of mammals and small reptiles that occasionally stole eggs or ate carrion.
Studies of teeth from northern Alaska suggest that northern populations of Troodon grew to a larger average body size than southern populations, hinting at Bergmann's rule.

A study of multiple Troodon teeth found in Upper Cretaceous deposits in northern Alaska found them much larger than those from southern localities, providing evidence that Alaskan populations reached a larger body size.
The study suggests Alaskan Troodon may have preyed on large animals because that habitat likely lacked large tyrannosaurs to compete for resources.
Troodon is considered a nomen dubium because its holotype consists of only a single tooth.
Troodon has historically been an unstable classification and has been subject to numerous conflicting synonymies with similar theropod specimens.
Troodon lived during the Campanian to Maastrichtian stages, from 83.6 to 66 million years ago.
Troodon fossils date to the Late Cretaceous, specifically the Campanian stage, with possible records from the Late Maastrichtian stage.
The environment where Troodon lived experienced temperatures between 2-12°C (36-54°F) and approximately 120 days of winter darkness.
